findings.where: First screen, the lede and the area around the 'Write to me directly' action (also missing everywhere below the fold)
findings.fault: Nothing near the one action shows that Mark has done this work, for whom, or where. The lede says whom he advises but names no body he has worked for, no region and no place or year (the brief already lists Melbourne 2026, Istanbul 2025 and São Paulo 2024). The page asks for an email before giving any proof beyond a face and an opinion.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a development bank who choose advisors against terms of reference. Before writing to a stranger they need to know he has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs, in their region (first-visit-trust items 3 and 6, 'what a visitor must be sure of'). Here they have to leave the page, for LinkedIn or the Profile page, to find out.

findings.where: First screen, the hero photograph as keyed onto the slate ground (and the 'Graded for the site' version in Texture)
findings.fault: The grade keys out the whole event backdrop, so 'Mark at work' becomes a cut-out head and shoulders floating on navy. Only the edge of a microphone hints that he is speaking anywhere. The one trust cue this direction was built on, Mark seen speaking at a real event, is gone, and the hand-cut edge around his hair and shoulder reads as a paste-up, not a portrait.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose v7 card asks for a full-bleed photograph of Mark speaking, as proof that he is asked to speak. Also a first-time visitor from a bank, for whom a photo at a named event is evidence (feel the CV) and a visible cut-out looks home-made.

findings.where: Footer, and the article specimen's byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024'
findings.fault: A visitor who lands on an article, the usual way in from a LinkedIn post, is never told who Mark is. Neither the byline nor the footer carries a one-line bio, only his name and address.
findings.who_objects: A reader at a development agency who followed a shared article. They see an opinion by a name they don't know, with nothing saying he is an infrastructure and PPP advisor to development banks and governments, so they can't tell whether writing to him makes sense (first-visit-trust item 12).

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026'
findings.fault: The newest talk, the strongest current proof on the page, shows a date but no venue or host. It tells the visitor that Mark spoke, but not who asked him.
findings.who_objects: Bank and agency staff, who judge standing by who invited the advisor ('feel the CV': the newest talk with its venue). A bare date is easy to skip.

findings.where: Navigation at the top: Profile · Articles and talks · Blog
findings.fault: The navigation has no 'Contact' label. On the homepage the blue action covers it, but on every other page the only way to reach Mark is the address in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading an article or the profile who decides to get in touch. They look for Contact at the top, where the house rule puts it ('a Contact label in the navigation'), and don't find it.
